topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease

audits.title: 295 Secondary Prevention of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Patients Admitted Under the Vascular Service - Full Cycle Audit
audits.standard: NICE CG147 and TA607 for peripheral arterial disease
audits.setting: Vascular Surgery Department, Doncaster and Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant 100%; lipid modification 82%; diabetic referral for high HbA1c 75%; smoking cessation advice/documentation 19%.

audits.intervention: Single teaching session for junior doctors and a dedicated computer for the vascular morning ward round.

cycle2.result: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant 100%; lipid modification 26 (96%); diabetic referral 100%; smoking cessation 100%.

audits.citation: Abadi P, Forsyth J, Drury D. 295 Secondary Prevention of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Patients Admitted Under the Vascular Service - Full Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.033.

audits.title: 145 Best Medical Therapy for Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Project in Vascular Surgery, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
audits.standard: NICE: best medical therapy with high-dose statin (atorvastatin 80mg) and antiplatelet for PAD; standard 100%
audits.setting: Vascular department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, NHS Grampian

cycle1.result: 28% (n=7) on BMT on admission, 40% (n=10) on discharge; 100% (n=25) on antiplatelet and 28% (n=7) on high-dose statin.

audits.intervention: New admission document prompting antiplatelet and statin review, plus departmental teaching on BMT.

cycle2.result: 25% (n=5) on BMT on admission, 80% (n=16) on discharge; 100% (n=20) on antiplatelet and 80% (n=16) on high-dose statin.

audits.other_findings: Low BMT rates on admission suggest poor implementation in primary care.
audits.citation: Hapca S, Shepherd J, Messeder S. 145 Best Medical Therapy for Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Project in Vascular Surgery, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.084.

audits.title: 54 Evaluating Best Medical Therapy Provision in Peripheral Arterial Disease Patients: A Prospective Audit
audits.standard: Best medical therapy for PAD: diabetes and hypertension control, statin, antiplatelet, exercise and smoking cessation advice
audits.setting: Vascular unit, ward admissions and vascular clinics (University Hospital Ayr)

cycle1.result: 4 of 11 smokers given cessation advice; all clinic patients given exercise advice; only 5 of 12 who should have had an antiplatelet received one; statins started in 7 of 14 not on one; 32 had lipid profile checked

audits.other_findings: 3 patients never had HbA1c checked; 7 of 14 poorly controlled diabetics had medication changed; neither newly diagnosed hypertensive patient was prescribed treatment.
audits.citation: Ishak P, Iftikhar N, Nadarasa A, Boom S, Wallace D. 54 Evaluating Best Medical Therapy Provision in Peripheral Arterial Disease Patients: A Prospective Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.524.

audits.title: 401 Cardiovascular Risk Factor Optimisation Amongst Inpatients with Peripheral Artery Disease – a Single-Centre Audit
audits.standard: NICE secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease (smoking cessation, lipid modification, antiplatelet therapy, blood pressure control, diabetes risk assessment); target 100%
audits.setting: St George's Vascular Institute, tertiary referral vascular surgery centre, inpatients

cycle1.result: Smoking cessation 40.5%, lipid modification 18.8%, blood pressure control 29.5%, diabetes risk assessment 21.1%, antiplatelet therapy 38.9%.

audits.other_findings: Admissions over 10 days had higher adherence (35.5% vs 19.8%, p=0.017); shorter elective admissions had worse optimisation.
audits.citation: Kawka M, Camelio M, Farrell–Dillon K, Howie S, Abdelhamid M, Moxey P, et al.. 401 Cardiovascular Risk Factor Optimisation Amongst Inpatients with Peripheral Artery Disease – a Single-Centre Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.232.

audits.title: 1065 Beyond the Incision: Optimising Secondary Prevention Prescriptions for Vascular Surgery Admissions Through a Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: Guidance-based secondary prevention with antiplatelets and statins
audits.setting: Vascular surgery department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Antiplatelets started by discharge in 36% of those admitted without antiplatelet or anticoagulant; statins started in 20% of those without lipid-lowering therapy; 15% discharged on no secondary prevention.

audits.intervention: Education on guidance-based secondary prevention and modification of the daily handover proforma to monitor prescribing

cycle2.result: Antiplatelet initiation 55% and statin initiation 41% in eligible patients; 13% discharged on no secondary prevention.

audits.other_findings: On admission 70% (pre) and 49% (post) were already on antithrombotic plus statin therapy.
audits.citation: Ekkunagul T, Francis J, Ngwira W, Drever S, MacLeod C, Renwick B. 1065 Beyond the Incision: Optimising Secondary Prevention Prescriptions for Vascular Surgery Admissions Through a Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.

audits.title: 1051 Audit of Statin Optimisation in Peripheral Arterial Disease and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysmal Disease
audits.setting: Vascular surgery inpatients, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Trust; PAD and AAA

audits.title: 1058 Evaluating Comprehensive Best Medical Therapy and Lifestyle Optimisation in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: An Integrated Audit of Adherence to ESVS 2023 Cardiovascular Standards and Global Vascular Guideline Recommendations
audits.standard: ESVS 2023 guidelines and Global Vascular Guidelines: antiplatelet, high-intensity statin, lipid profile, BP <140/90, smoking cessation advice, HbA1c within 3 months
audits.setting: Vascular inpatients, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Statin 80%; antiplatelet 60%; lipid profile 1/34 (2.9%); discharge BP at target 29/35 (82.9%); smoking cessation documented 5/36 (13.9%); HbA1c within 3 months 14/49 (28.6%).

audits.other_findings: Structured pathways, automated prompts and routine lifestyle documentation were proposed.
audits.citation: Miah M, Bara A, Mahajan S, Ragavan S, Riaz M, Ogar L, et al.. 1058 Evaluating Comprehensive Best Medical Therapy and Lifestyle Optimisation in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: An Integrated Audit of Adherence to ESVS 2023 Cardiovascular Standards and Global Vascular Guideline Recommendations. audits.title: 742 Improving Cardiovascular Risk Optimisation in Vascular Surgery Patients: A Two-Cycle Audit of Adherence to VSGBI Standards
audits.standard: VSGBI cardiovascular risk reduction framework: BMT, gastroprotection, HbA1c and lipid assessment

cycle1.result: Antiplatelet 124/153 (81.1%); anticoagulation 60/153 (39.2%); statin 122/153 (79.7%); gastroprotection 54/153 (35.3%); HbA1c 27/153 (17.7%); lipid profile 19/153 (12.4%).

audits.intervention: Surgical team teaching sessions and departmental posters.

cycle2.result: Antiplatelet 50/60 (83.3%); anticoagulation 30/60 (50.0%); statin 48/60 (80.0%); gastroprotection 40/60 (66.7%); HbA1c 18/60 (30.0%); lipid profile 39/60 (65.0%).

audits.other_findings: Most admissions were for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia and diabetic foot infection.
audits.citation: Majid S, Lim J, Young E, Lang A, Young J, Botros K, et al.. 742 Improving Cardiovascular Risk Optimisation in Vascular Surgery Patients: A Two-Cycle Audit of Adherence to VSGBI Standards. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.775.

audits.title: Improving Compliance with Statins in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Vascular Society of Great Britain and Ireland and draft NICE guidance: all patients undergoing major vascular procedures should be prescribed a statin
audits.setting: Vascular team, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Statins not prescribed in 30.1% of discharge letters (113 admissions, 96 patients)

audits.intervention: Several junior doctor-led interventions monitored through weekly PDSA cycles (details not stated)

cycle2.result: Statins not prescribed in 24.4% (86 admissions, 76 patients), an 18.9% decrease

audits.other_findings: Poorly compliant subgroups were patients with embolism and those having elective angioplasty.
audits.citation: Agha RA, Camm CF, Edison E, Browning N. Improving Compliance with Statins in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Study. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2012;1:30-33. doi:10.1016/s2049-0801(12)70010-9. PMID: 26257905.

audits.title: An audit of secondary prevention for peripheral arterial disease in primary care - scope for improved collaboration between vascular surgery and general practitioners.
audits.standard: Best medical therapy: antiplatelets, statins, smoking cessation, blood pressure and glycaemic control
audits.setting: GP Healthlink referrals to vascular surgery, University College Hospital Galway (Saolta region)

cycle1.result: 34.5% (n = 40) on antiplatelets and 52% (n = 60) on statins; 31% no smoking status; only eleven letters mentioned risk factor optimisation

audits.intervention: Information leaflet on best medical therapy posted to all GP practices (re-audit planned at 6 months)
audits.other_findings: Suspected critical limb ischaemia not associated with BMT prescription (p = 0.664); 28% active smokers.
audits.citation: Foley MP, Tubassam M, Walsh SR. An audit of secondary prevention for peripheral arterial disease in primary care - scope for improved collaboration between vascular surgery and general practitioners. Ir J Med Sci. 2023;192(6):3007-3010. doi:10.1007/s11845-023-03362-1. PMID: 37099256.
